fields.title: Employee count cannot be confirmed — third-party sources conflict
fields.claim: The company is described — by itself and by third parties — as a small, unusually capital-efficient team.
fields.what-we-know: Verification question, not a conclusion: third-party estimates range from ~250 to 1,200+ employees, and the org chart received redacts totals. Nothing here suggests wrongdoing; the number is simply unconfirmed.
fields.impact: Headcount drives burn and the ARR-per-employee figures used in the thesis. IC should rely on neither until a primary source lands.

fields.title: Revenue figures are unaudited and the ARR definition is unclear
fields.claim: ARR of ~$200M was reported for Sep 2025, and the founder later stated ~$500M 'annualised' revenue on X (Mar 2026).
fields.what-we-know: Open verification question: both figures are reported or company-stated. No audited or management accounts have been received — the audited-financials request is Blocked — and whether the $500M figure is contracted ARR, a run-rate month or gross bookings is undefined in the sources held.
fields.impact: The valuation discussion is anchored on these numbers. Any term sheet should condition on receipt and review of management accounts.

fields.title: Reported valuation is roughly 100x reported ARR — a terms question
fields.claim: A ~$20B valuation (Sep 2025 reports) against ~$200M reported ARR implies a multiple near 100x.
fields.what-we-know: Noted as a terms question, not a conclusion: both sides of the multiple are reported figures (see Evidence), so the multiple is arithmetic on unverified inputs. It frames the pricing discussion; it does not settle it.
fields.impact: Pricing and structure — preference stack, ratchets, tranching — are where this gets resolved. Flagged for the IC discussion and the prior-terms request.
